summary: "Tests whether LLMs can control their own internal representations. A prior study applied neurofeedback to LLMs and claimed they can, but its control targets were not privileged (a third party could infer them from the prompt). This work redesigns the neurofeedback paradigm so the control target satisfies the privileged-access requirement, closer to human neurofeedback experiments. Under this stricter setting, models do not demonstrate reliable control over privileged internal representations, indicating that rigorous assessments of LLM metacognition require evaluation methods that demand privileged access."
findings:
  - "Identifies that previously reported \"control\" of internal representations may rely on superficial mechanisms because targets were not privileged"
  - "Redesigns the neurofeedback paradigm for LLMs with a privileged-access requirement (fixed output sentence, scalar probe-based feedback, scoring rule never revealed)"
  - "Shows current models struggle to control privileged internal representations, with implications for AI safety and metacognition evaluation"
